newsitem.title: INDIA: Suspected Indian rebels bomb train, 400 unhurt.
newsitem.headline: Suspected Indian rebels bomb train, 400 unhurt.

text.p: More than 400 passengers escaped unhurt when suspected tribal guerrillas set off a remote-control bomb on a rail track in the northeastern Indian state of Assam on Monday, derailing six coaches, police said.
There was no immediate report of casualties in the blast, which police said must have occurred a couple of minutes before the train reached the spot.
The Rajdhani Express train was passing through Barpeta district, about 100 km (60 miles) west of the state's main city, Guwahati, when the crudely-made bomb exploded, police said.
All passengers on the train, which was on its way to Delhi from Guwahati, were brought back safely to Guwahati, railway spokeswoman Leena Sharma told Reuters.
"We suspect the Bodoland Liberation Tigers Force (BLTF) to be involved in the blast as they have been bombing bridges in the state for the last couple of days," a senior police official said.
The BLTF, who are seeking a separate province carved out of Assam for 600,000 Bodo tribespeople, bombed a train on December 30 last year, killing at least 30 passengers.
Monday's blast came two days before the start of a planned 36-hour general strike by Bodo student groups campaigning for a Bodoland province.
Bodo guerrillas have killed 11 people in the past two weeks in Assam with remote-control bombs, police said.

Police said they recovered wires and bottles, apparently used in making the bomb, from the site of the blast. Security forces had launched a combing operation to track down the guerrillas who engineered the blast, they said.
